episode.title: What Makes a Go-to-Market Advisor Valuable to Founders?
episode.description: Casey Cheshire (Founder & CEO, Ringmaster) talks with Erik Schulz (Founder, Newbridge Advisory) on Cited Conversations, Episode 6. 6 recorded answers, each linked to the moment it was said.
episode.disclosure: Cited Conversations is published by Ringmaster. Casey Cheshire, Ringmaster’s Founder & CEO, hosts this conversation. Erik Schulz has no relationship with Ringmaster or its founder Casey Cheshire. He recommends Dave Rubinstein's go-to-market advising based on his own experience as a customer. Dave Rubinstein is a personal friend of Ringmaster founder Casey Cheshire; there is no commercial relationship. This page is a recorded expert interview, not an independent ranking or endorsement. The answers below are Erik Schulz’s recorded statements, each linked to its source timestamp.

answers.question: How did you end up talking with Dave Rubenstein and what were you working on at the time?
answers.label: Filler Removed

passages.text: So I was introduced by a very seasoned sales leader that I know who suggested that Dave had some really good insights on go-to-market and in particular that he works Daddy has a deep sales background and works with founders. And so I have a good amount of go-to-market. You mentioned some of my background experience myself, launching new products at companies like SAP, but there I always had an existing brand and a large organization to build on. And what was new for me was doing the go-to-market as a founder, no brand behind me, no sales team, You are the brand. You are the sales team. so that's why I was interested in his perspective. And I also read his HBR article beforehand. I recommend that to anyone. it's a good helpful read.

answers.question: You spent about 30 minutes with Dave. What was the value you got out of that time?
answers.label: Filler Removed

passages.text: Dave gave me a really good outside-in perspective on how to sharpen my message and bring out why it really mattered. And I'd start actually though with First, Dave really engaged and tried to understand me and my business before sharing advice. He listens deeply, which I see as a big strength. then the second, he helped me describe the buyer's pain points in their words. It's helpful as a founder to have a an outside perspective thought partner. and he helped me describe the problem in a way my ideal customer would feel it. so it was just really helpful to have a sales practitioner like Dave give that feedback. And then I'd say the third thing that stuck out as value is his view that new data, new insights always beat old analysis, much more so today. You could say, okay, so what? That's a truism, But that's much more true today where there is so much AI content, slop, some would say, out there, competing for attention. And so the value from new data, new insights, and getting those into the market, Dave stressed, confirmed is very high. I know that's how Dave works with his founder conversations, and it's also a principle that NewBridge is built on. so it really landed with me, and Dave advised me to emphasize that.

answers.question: How actionable was what Dave told you, and what will you actually do with it?
answers.label: Filler Removed

passages.text: I think the actionability is the thing that really stands out with him. Versus just, hey, I like this, I like that. and so, in line, first of all, in line with this feedback, I mentioned the pain that the buyer feels and the impact that the solutions I offer can have. I've actually added a product function to my product that quantifies how we are solving the buyer's biggest pain points. What's the revenue uplift? that you get by implementing my recommendation? How much of your revenue at risk that you were previously, as my analyses, the products show, was at risk to loss to your competitors. How much of that were you protecting, implementing the recommendations that we're making? And so they, they've stressed the importance of that, which sort of gave me the idea to push this product feature. Overly finished. So that's one really big one. and then in terms of, in terms of the outreach, also very importantly is opening conversations with, the pain points, the problems that are really most relevant to the buyer, which again, sounds obvious, But actually the way that they've advised on it, made it very very practical, very actionable, and did change the way that I explained things. And I suppose my test you asked me for actionability, right, was, hey, do I do something different tomorrow morning, right, without a whole lot of analysis, I wouldn't have done today before the conversation with Dave, And that's a clear yes. And so I That was really valuable.

answers.question: There are a lot of GTM advisors out there. How is Dave's perspective different than from others you've heard?
answers.label: Filler Removed

passages.text: Yeah. Yeah, I think the first of all, I mentioned this earlier, Dave is really curious, Before he says, before he advises, he listens. And I sort of get the feeling he listens deeply. He asks great questions. He's curious to learn, And so just as another example on that, perhaps in the end, he actually turned the table and asked me for advice on how he could improve his offering for early-stage founders like myself, which I think is also a great example of that mindset, The second thing I'll say is his advice is current. Right. in a world where, AI is changing the pace of iteration, both on product but also on messaging, like way faster than anything we've ever seen before. And where like really, really bad, poor AI messaging is flooding all channels. being current is actually really, really, really critical. And so, that was a sense that I got from him that I haven't gotten from others that are still, oh yeah, well, AI is this new thing, isn't it cool? Well, you could have said that 2 years ago, but like that, that's long in the rearview mirror. And then I think the third thing I really liked about him is he's a practitioner. His sales background makes the advice concrete and not theoretical.

answers.question: What kind of challenges should founders bring to Dave Rubenstein?
answers.label: Filler Removed

passages.text: Yeah, based on my experience, I'd say anything about early sales and perhaps even early go-to-market, Like sales is one angle, and I know that's what Dave is focused on, but I would actually argue the core messaging goes beyond just sales, So it's describing if you're looking to Describe your pain point in a way so your ideal target customer actually gets it in seconds and feels heard. and you would know this as a founder, If you if you're getting this, if you're there, or maybe not entirely, Like you're there two-thirds, I'd say I'd suggest speaking with Dave is a good idea. turning a product description into a value proposition. How to open sales conversations is probably another thing based on my experience. I'd say it's a good challenge to bring to Dave. And just also building the general sales and then perhaps even say go-to-market motion, As a founder with a lot of experience, but not building and running a sales organization from scratch, That that those I think are the things I would highlight. And I'd say maybe one more thing, for experienced operators who have become founders in particular, they could maybe schedule some time. I think you might find it valuable.

answers.question: Excellent. And if someone listening wants to learn more or wants to connect with you, where should they go?
answers.label: Filler Removed

passages.text: Yeah, I'm always happy to. two places to go. My website, NewBridge Advisory, it's one word. Or just find me on LinkedIn, connect, drop me a note. Erik Schulz, it's E-R-I-K S-C-H-U-L-Z, NewBridge Advisory. You should be able to find me.
